questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord does not yet know of the defect (the tenant has not reported it and the landlord has not learned of it in another way)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the claim state that the tenant intends to pay the rent on deposit with the office designated by the canton instead of to the landlord, or has begun to do so?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the claim state that at least one rent payment has already been paid into deposit with the office designated by the canton?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the tenant claim compensation from the landlord for damage the defect caused to the tenant (for example damaged furniture or clothing, or extra costs)?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord learned of the defect only orally, so that no written notice, written acknowledgement or inspection record of it exists?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Does the claim state that the rented dwelling has a defect (for example mould, damp, or heating that fails) or that the tenant is disturbed in using the dwelling as agreed, without the claim itself saying that the tenant alone caused the defect or must remedy it at his own expense?

text:
Hi,

I rent a small flat from Bachtel Trading Ltd at Dorfstrasse 31 in Luzern, CHF 1050 a month, and I'm running out of patience with them.

Someone at work told me that instead of paying the rent to the landlord you can pay it into an account with the authorities until things get fixed. I keep going back and forth on that. Part of me thinks it's the only language they understand, part of me worries it will just make everything worse. I genuinely haven't settled on it either way.

The problem is the heating. Since the end of September the radiators in the living room and bedroom stay stone cold, only the one in the bathroom gets a bit warm. It's mid-October now and in the mornings it's 15 degrees inside. I sit at home in a jacket and sleep under two duvets.

When it started, on 25 September 2026, I phoned Ms Tara Palmer at Bachtel and told her exactly what was going on. A week later I ran into her in front of the building and told her again. Both times she said she would "see to it". That was all by word of mouth. I never put anything in writing, she never confirmed anything in writing either, and nobody has come round to look at the radiators.

What should I do now?

Thanks,
Paul Steiner
